verifications.claim: The Masters uses a sudden-death playoff format if golfers are tied after 72 holes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Masters has a sudden-death playoff format.'; R2: 'The Masters Tournament uses sudden death.'; R3: 'Augusta National goes sudden-death'; R4: 'standard sudden-death format'; R5: 'The Masters uses a sudden-death format'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly state the Masters uses sudden-death playoff for ties after 72 holes.

verifications.claim: Players immediately play the 18th hole in the Masters sudden-death playoff.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The first playoff hole is the 18th'; R2: 'playoff would start on the par-4 18th hole'; R3: 'Playoffs begin on No. 18'; R4: 'playoff participants will return to the 18th hole'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm the playoff starts immediately on the 18th hole.

verifications.claim: If still tied in the Masters sudden-death playoff, players proceed to the 10th hole.

verifications.claim: Players alternate between the 18th hole and the 10th hole in the Masters sudden-death playoff until a winner is decided.

verifications.claim: The sudden-death playoff format at the Masters has been used 12 times since 1979.
verifications.label: CLEAR
